newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia & Upjohn falls on Q3 EPS outlook.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn falls on Q3 EPS outlook.

text.p: Shares in Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc dropped 4-3/4 to 36-5/8 on heavy trading volume Friday after the company said it expected third-quarter earnings to be well below Wall Street expectations.
The Swedish-American drugs giant said it expects profits for the three months ended September 30 to total about $0.44 per share, on a pro forma basis, flat with year-ago results.
Wall Street had expected $0.54 per share, according to the First Call consensus of 24 analysts' forecasts.
"This had a big, big impact on the stock today," said independent pharmaceuticals analyst Hemant Shah.

In a statement from its London office, the company said third-quarter results were hurt by "negative foreign exchange developments, especially the effect of the weakened Japanese yen on sales. Additionally, a strengthened Swedish krona and Italian lira increased the cost of goods sold."

The company said it estimated quarterly sales were up two percent over last year, despite the foreign exchange impact, which reduced sales by about two percent. Also cited by the company were "continued pressure on prices and on sales of older products, particularly in the United States."

Moreover, the company said, "While the merger of Pharmacia AB and The Upjohn Company, which took place last November, is proceeding on target, the company noted that integration has caused the usual short-term disruptions seen in a multinational merger."
Pharmacia & Upjohn was formed through a merger of Pharmacia AB and Upjohn Co and began operating in November 1995.
